issues.title: P0 #328 follow-up — Preserve typed Windows Service busy without false durable source error
issues.body:
# Bounded product fix after #377 diagnosis — preserve request-level Service busy semantics

**Priority P0 candidate, ENGINEERING ONLY; BLOCKED until Owner accepts/merges #377 diagnosis**. Parent #328; diagnostics source PR [#377](https://github.com/ArdenZC/Zen-Canvas/pull/377). Owner source review [comment](https://github.com/ArdenZC/Zen-Canvas/pull/377#issuecomment-6106375094) conditionally PASS, exact combined-HEAD CI pending. This issue is not evidence of resolved historical SQLite lock or native C:/D:/E:/F: health.

## Proven issue at source/test level
`ServiceRuntime::try_begin_index_request` emits v3 `index_service_busy` for an overlapping index request, preserving global Service status `indexing` and no Service lifecycle error. `windows/service_errors.rs::decode` currently maps this typed code to untyped `GlobalIndexError::Provider`, and generic Coordinator error handling can persist `INDEX_STATUS_ERROR` after writing `SYNCING`. Test `busy_source_waits_for_a_new_wake_before_an_explicit_retry` starts READY, injects busy, observes ERROR, and proves only a later explicit wake recovers. Historic native cause **UNVERIFIED**, including SQLite writer identity and multi-volume failures.

## Engineering task for Codex Cloud after #377 merged
1. Start from exact current master **after #377 merge**. Verify source HEAD/tree and test source authority; do not write atop the old df37531 baseline, do not modify #377 PR, and do not duplicate its research report.
2. Decode `index_service_busy` exclusively from the existing **trusted v3 error_code** into a narrow typed *request-level contention* variant distinct from SQLite BUSY, permission_required, paused, rebuild_required and permanent provider/source failures. Do not classify by message text or loosen protocol validation. Assess exhaustive matches/callers and service-level transitions.
3. In the **per-source** Coordinator result path distinguish request not admitted vs provider actually failed; prevent a competing busy rejection from being durably recorded as source `error` or erasing a genuinely committed degraded source status. Preserve already-committed source identity/generation, checkpoints and prior health; do not mark READY or advance timestamps/checkpoints based on busy. Carefully handle the fact that Coordinator writes `SYNCING/INDEXING` **before** invoking provider; avoid leaving indefinite artificial 'syncing' state when no real owner will finish it. Require explicit, coherent projection/repair contract (e.g. preserve/restore last committed status conditionally with revision guard) rather than simplistic 'skip error write'. Review stale/out-of-order response and state ownership.
4. Add deterministic contract tests traversing actual v3 Service response decode **through Coordinator behavior** where possible; test initial/Resume/Rebuild, same and different sources, busy then successful existing wake, multiple-volume per-source isolation, actual permission/IO/SQLite faults, paused/rebuild-required, cancelled/shutdown, old/new checkpoints and source status truth. Ensure tests fail on old behavior and pass on repair. No flakiness/reliance on sleeping.
5. Use existing event-driven source/coordinator/wake mechanisms only; **no automatic retry loops, generic increasing busy_timeout, polling, new worker/queue/source authority, schema migration, IPC field/version change, LocalSystem privilege expansion, source bulk deletes, AI or Index Scope change**. If a safe correction requires broader recovery authority, STOP and return an exact guardrail escalation before widening.
6. Run focused Rust checks and current required Windows/macOS Hosted CI at exact PR HEAD; preserve failure/cancellation history. Windows physical machine is Owner native acceptance only, not development. No Codex Review.
7. Open standalone **Draft PR** scoped to minimal production handler/error mapping + tests, and deliver final SHA/tree, source diff, CI, explicit behavior invariant and UNVERIFIED native status. No merge before Owner manual review.

## Completion criteria
`REQUEST-LEVEL SERVICE BUSY CORRECTLY TYPED AND NO FALSE DURABLE SOURCE ERROR — HOSTED PASS / NATIVE UNVERIFIED` when tested; only post-merge and actual Windows evidence can finish #328.

issues.title: P1 Managed Scan — root-aware exclusion correctness and lossless state repair
issues.body:
# P1 Managed Scan path/root-aware filter correction — Owner-scoped production follow-up

**Parent evidence:** #375; test-only Draft [PR #378](https://github.com/ArdenZC/Zen-Canvas/pull/378), Owner source review [comment](https://github.com/ArdenZC/Zen-Canvas/pull/378#issuecomment-6107140464). **Do not begin implementation until #378 has been reconciled, merged and exact post-merge master checks accepted by Owner.** ChatGPT/Owner owns architecture, source research and product-policy definition; Codex Cloud only implements/tests an approved bounded code change. This is distinct from Global Index Scope / ADR-0014 and must not launch production Global Index policy.

## Proven defect boundary
- Name-only exclusions used in scanner, watcher and db query/path upsert prevent newly created valuable user files under `Projects/Windows`, `Design/build`, `Configs/AppData` from reaching `scan_seen`/File Library even though scan completes healthy and root reports healthy.
- Explicitly selected `.../build` root cannot scan/watch README; bulk upsert may accept it. Inconsistent scope authority.
- Previously indexed ignored-subtree entries can stay query-visible, without stale reconciliation, even if no longer on disk. New generic cleanup could destroy user state, so no blanket deletion.
- Existing exclusion for actual OS-managed directories, recognized dependency/build/cache trees and IDE metadata still has valid resource/safety motives; the report is not permission to index Windows system files or all `node_modules`.

## Engineering contract for later Codex Cloud task
1. Define a shared **path+selected-root+source-identity** exclusion decision used by Managed Scan traversal, Watcher event handling, bulk upsert and stale-reconciliation protection, with an explicit ordered precedence and deterministic reason codes. Keep Mac and Win OS-specific root/known-folder identity; do **not** exempt a path solely because a basename is `Windows`, `build`, `AppData`, or `Program Files`. No platform hardcoded arbitrary / OS privilege bypass.
2. A user-selected root receives a truthful coverage decision before scanning. Preserve explicitly authorized user roots and ordinary user data under lookalike child names, while refusing unsafe/privileged system-protected paths when necessary. Maintain source authority, symlink/junction boundary, case normalization, volume identity and folder exceptions.
3. Keep recognized dependency trees `node_modules`, `.venv`, IDE metadata `.vscode`, generated outputs and cache defaults unless a separate Owner-approved user override explicitly says otherwise. Make generated-build classification based on project signatures and path context, not generic any-folder-named-`build`.
4. Ensure Managed Scan, Watcher, bulk upsert and stale reconciliation share the same decision for the same context. Preserve previously committed file identities, user tags/notes/corrections and stale history; DO NOT blindly mark every previously ignored subtree stale, delete records, VACUUM or bulk reindex without approved migration/preview/rollback.
5. Regression suite MUST show old false-exclusion assertions intentionally **changed to desired coverage** (not merely passed as characterization) for user paths `Projects/Windows/README.md`, `Design/build/logo.ai`, `Configs/AppData/important.json` and explicitly selected `.../build` root. Verify actual system Windows/AppData and recognized dependencies remain excluded by correct authority. Test case/Unicode/extended path, selected root precedence, Watcher real handling where Hosted allows, multi-root behavior, filesystem permission boundaries and both ordinary and previously ignored stale handling. Preserve existing #375 characterization evidence as historical record; do not silently delete tests.
6. No impact on Global Index provider/MFT/USN/Spotlight, Search P95/benchmark, Schema/IPC, AI eligibility, consent, mutation authority or default new Index Scope. No performance threshold relaxation, no extra service, watcher, polling or repeated scanning. No Codex Review, no Windows-local coding.
7. A separate Draft PR with exact HEAD/tree, check matrix and safety report requires manual ChatGPT/Owner review and Hosted Windows/macOS CI; native Owner acceptance before making claims about real Watcher/OS directory identity. If the 'known OS root' identity/selected-root override contract cannot be implemented safely without changing policy, stop and escalate to Owner before writing production filter code.

## Owner acceptance scope
Phase 1 is a **correctness repair for existing Managed Scan** and suppression of false exclusions, not activation of ISG-02/03 Global Index Scope governance, AI, or cleanup. **Outcome when done**: user-designated valuable directories indexed and watched while genuine protected/system/dependency paths retain safe defaults and old stored state is lossless.

**Source-grounded Owner architecture review complete.** A standalone Markdown decision/validation contract, `Zen_Canvas_380_K2_Activation_and_Upgrade_Isolation_Contract_2026-10-13.md`, has been authored in the Owner conversation (NOT yet committed to GitHub). Exact-HEAD #389 ordinary CI 38349343362 SUCCESS but does not execute K1 native/harness qualification. #380 remains OPEN.

**Product-source facts controlling K2:**
- `src-tauri/src/lib.rs:135-150`: normal DB path `app_data_dir()/zen-canvas.sqlite3`, QA override exists only under feature flag.
- `src-tauri/src/db/connection.rs:79-100,213-220`: creates SQL pool, initializes WAL/NORMAL and calls full `migrate(&conn)` before `Database::open` returns; post-open flags are too late.
- `src-tauri/src/main.rs:58-110,158-245`: single-instance plugin is registered, then Tauri setup first opens DB and runs recovery/prune before coordinator/AI/Watcher. Single-instance is not a cross-generation OS enforcement proof.
- `src-tauri/windows/installer-lifecycle-final.nsh:38-132`: exact-owned service stop followed by a **name-only** desktop Find/Kill/500ms recheck and Preview quiesce. One-time check does not prove a continuously closed startup window.
- `src-tauri/src/global_index/windows/service_host.rs:1-15`: Service mainly enumerates/streams over IPC; the Desktop Sink and independent workers/Direct path own DB-related effects, so SCM STOPPED is not a complete DB writer fence.

**Owner decisions:** (1) S-only shared-path plus one-time stop-world: **NO-GO**; (2) N-only physically separate path plus snapshot/pointer: **NO-GO** because late writes fork user state and old binary can still act on user files; (3) **H HYBRID as conditional design candidate only**: independent pre-open activation authority, provably persistent old actor exclusion including already-open handles and late relaunch, last-write/WAL-complete snapshot, verified physical distinct DB generation, seal/data-preserving offline migration, durable crash-recoverable activation ledger, new-epoch connection/Service/Direct/worker checks, forward recovery and strict no-silent-fork policy. Three separate version authorities must remain distinct: installation activation, DB write generation, and C2/#381 domain publication epochs.

**Critical feasibility qualification:** an unmodified old app does not obey a new mutex, pre-open marker, version flag or Service protocol; it may still have OS permissions to operate ordinary user files. Physical DB separation cannot universally prevent old native file operations. If the product requirement is *absolute prevention of any old same-user binary operating on personal files*, that cannot be claimed without OS-enforced authority over those objects and live native proof. Do not silently weaken the product promise. If legacy lifetime exclusion cannot be proven, automatic migration must **BLOCK** rather than creating two active databases. A new-only ACL/registry record/user_version/one-time KillProcess does not count as enforcement.

**K2 draft includes:** 12 safety invariants (preopen, noncooperative legacy, physical DB identity, last writer, committed WAL, no silent fork, unique active generation, prepublish preservation, FK/rowid/history, recovery, no automatic Schema-37 downgrade, native file identity), candidate activation state machine, six-phase cutover/rollback, Windows and macOS risk boundaries, old×new matrix and eight K2-T0 future test gates.

Core aim: demonstrate or refute **continuously enforceable exclusion of unchanged old SQLite writers through snapshot/cutover and new activation**, alias/WAL/handle/relaunch and actual Windows/macOS native OS authority boundaries. Test-only Windows hosted evidence is not Owner native proof; avoid redundant K1/Track A/B and #381 inventories. Never manufacture a PASS from a mocked stop-world. Stop at `K2_T0_TEST_ONLY_READY_FOR_OWNER_REVIEW` or `K2_T0_OS_AUTHORITY_BLOCKED`. Production implementation, Schema v38 allocation, IPC/installer/Service edits, Full CI/100k/500k/1m, native Owner-machine development, Codex Review, merge, Issue close and release are not authorized.

## OWNER #380 K1 — DB-OPEN ISOLATION TEST-ONLY EVIDENCE ACCEPTED / S AND N PRODUCTION NO-GO (2026-10-13)

Independently reviewed remote [Draft PR #389](https://github.com/ArdenZC/Zen-Canvas/pull/389), the full K1 report, frozen-source extraction/build and test/actor modules, committed structured event and source-provenance records, the 20-method test output, and GitHub CI/PR metadata. **This is an evidence/source review, NOT an independent local rerun or native Windows qualification.**

**Exact Git identity:** Branch `test/issue-380-k1-db-open-generation` HEAD `bbdd3db254582ae622236237b87adb73b097bc42` / Tree `6341a9fdf547fe85331121a412fcb35622415bda`; sole parent and unchanged remote master `3275ac7c72df8ae4139a30f16c7f649971324e97` / master tree `009576241cd4e8e2ba12cc644a368314f599faa6`. Compare ahead 1/behind 0; exactly **23 newly added files, +5063/-0**, restricted to `tests/issue380_db_open_generation/**` and `docs/research/ISSUE-380-K1-DB-OPEN-ISOLATION-RESULT.md`. PR #389 remains OPEN/Draft. No production, Schema 37, Service/IPC, NSIS, workflow, #381 or master changes.

**CI updated since Codex handoff:** [exact-HEAD run 38349343362](https://github.com/ArdenZC/Zen-Canvas/actions/runs/38349343362), attempt 1, is now **COMPLETED / SUCCESS**. Independently inspected 27 jobs: **7 success, 20 expected conditionally skipped, 0 failed/cancelled**. Quality Windows/macOS and scope/routing succeed; K1's Python/Rust probe harness and Windows native SCM/NSIS/old-app matrix were **NOT** executed by CI. Never promote ordinary CI quality success to K1 Hosted Windows qualification. No CI rerun needed.

**Executed isolated evidence accepted in its actual boundary:** Committed `unittest.stdout.txt` reports **20/20 PASS** across K1-01..K1-09 and `results.json` records **269 structured events** with `methods_run=20,success=true`. The frozen `Database::open`, `configure_connection`, Schema 37 migration DDL, DB path functions and old/new fallback bodies are extracted from pinned source with hashes; probe compiles offline using Rust 1.97.1 and rusqlite bundled **SQLite 3.51.3** and actually opens/migrates disposable SQLite files. A fresh opener records **v37 / 65 persistent tables / 5000ms busy timeout**; open/migrate completes before a hypothetical later admission rejection. A same-version reopen can execute persistent DDL. The independent Python 3.12/SQLite 3.53.1 legacy actor is a behavioral substitute, **not an old Zen Canvas Desktop binary, installed Service or pipe peer**. Tauri path acquisition, default settings and transport classification are mocked. POSIX symlink/flock/atomic rename and process-exit tests are not Windows NSIS/SCM, power-loss or native loaded-image evidence.

**Observed S (one fixed DB path) negative witnesses:** Retained and reconnected old SQLite actor writes before/after new opener; setting an incompatible future user_version causes the *new opener* to reject but cannot revoke an already-open old connection; old reads keep a valid WAL snapshot; a mock Service-stop or one-time Close does not prevent late independently launched old actors; new-only POSIX advisory lock is ignored by non-participating legacy actor; actual opener returns BUSY after its frozen 5s timeout but old writer can subsequently write. Thus **S current one-time-close/new-only-lock design NO-GO**. Do not claim this proves a properly enforced native lifetime stop-world is impossible; such enforcement has simply not been demonstrated.

**Observed N (separate DB namespace/cutover) negative witnesses:** Lexical namespace can alias the same inode; copying SQLite main DB without WAL misses a committed change, whereas online backup captures it; writes after a correct snapshot do not reach the new DB; after simulated pointer switching the old/new processes independently commit divergent corrections, and the old process still executes an actual owned-file rename; restart/profile/restore can choose fixed old path or older data. POSIX process-exit pointer replacement proves only whole-file outcomes, not power-loss-safe Windows activation. Isolated 36→37 successful/error rollback and representative **three-row, 17-domain-table + FTS/FK/rowid/history** snapshot projections are limited positives, not migration/scale qualification. **N alone NO-GO**. Generation-separated paths are at most defense-in-depth until non-cooperative old writers/native file actions, last-write cutover, path identity and rollback are controlled.

**Recorded provenance caveat:** `evidence/results.json` has `environment.head` = frozen master because the committed evidence was generated *before* the K1 commit; it also records hash-bound test inputs, source manifest and source slices. The PR author states a final-HEAD rerun passed but its updated artifacts stayed ignored/uncommitted. Treat the committed log as **hash-bound precommit local execution**, and the final exact-HEAD Actions success as **quality/routing only**. Do not claim a committed exact-PR-head K1 harness rerun or fresh independent test execution. This does not invalidate the accepted negative witnesses, and does not justify an expensive new Hosted run.

**OWNER DISPOSITION:** `#380-K1_TEST_ONLY_EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED / S_CURRENT_PRODUCTION_NO_GO / N_STANDALONE_PRODUCTION_NO_GO / PRE_OPEN_LIFETIME_ISOLATION_UNPROVEN / K1_HOSTED_WINDOWS_NOT_RUN / OWNER_NATIVE_UNVERIFIED / #389_OPEN_DRAFT_MERGE_HOLD / #385_MERGE_HOLD / #386_INDEPENDENT_MERGE_NO_GO / #388_MERGE_HOLD / #381_D4_PRODUCTION_HOLD / SCHEMA_V38_UNALLOCATED / NSIS_U2_RELEASE_NO_GO`.

**Next architecture decision, Owner-owned, not a Codex production assignment:** specify an enforceable pre-open activation boundary for *unmodified* legacy binaries, continuous Desktop/Service/worker/native-file-operation exclusion through final snapshot and new writer admission, an authenticated physical DB namespace/complete WAL cutover, recoverable activation ledger and no-loss rollback/forward-recovery. Compare a verifiable OS-level stop-world and isolated active-generation DB as a combined operating protocol rather than forcing S-only vs N-only. Identify native Windows and macOS proof gates before any production implementation authorization. This is a bounded architecture choice, not permission to launch K1 reruns, new research PRs, Schema migration or production code.
